commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 generalize (PR #1300): decouples component gates from exemplar flags; PR body says the witness's exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" — logic/scope correction to 100 merged generated modules.
description: `section_122_component_rate` is gated on `entry_is_section_122_exempt` / `entry_is_section_232_covered` — never again zeroed by China-list or aluminum membership (the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins)

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The section 122 surcharge exclusion branch tested the witness exemplar flags `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b` instead of the source's 9903.03.03 exclusion list and section 232-covered metal articles, zeroing the surcharge for China-301-list and aluminum lines of every origin.
triage.triage_notes: Chapter 51; same pattern as index 48, diff read in full (26 redundant paren pairs, `from:` spelling). Same six re-gated rules, same two added steel rules, same statutory-stack addend; index 48 caveats apply.
triage.verifier_justification: The refutation attempts fail: the diff changes encoded meaning (formula tokens in `section_122_component_rate.versions[1]`, plus new parameter/derived rules and a new term in `schedule_statutory_stack`), so it is neither mechanical nor test-only, and the pre-state was genuinely wrong rather than merely narrow. The rule's proof atoms are identical before and after and claim grounding in the Proclamation 11012 exclusion clauses ("subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04"), which I confirmed through the pinned release: FR 2026-03824 para (2) excludes "articles listed in paragraph 2 of Annex I ... and as enumerated in Annex II" and para (4) says the surcharge "shall not apply in addition to tariffs imposed under section 232" — nothing in the source excludes §301-listed or aluminum-membership lines. Yet the pre formula gated the exclusion on `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b`, the same booleans this very file uses as the China-301 list-1 gate (`if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate`) and the aluminum/§232 gate, so in chapter 51 (wool) the branch suppressed the 10% surcharge on a population with no source basis, for every origin. The fix re-grounds the branch to the atoms' own provisions (`entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered`), which is exactly untraceable_branch ("a branch... with no basis in the cited source... the fix removes or re-grounds it"), not a boundary, amount, polarity, or entity/period defect.
triage.verifier_notes:
Source verification (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, corpus commit e79781bd): Proclamation 11012 (us/rulemaking/federal-register/2026-02-25/2026-03824) para (2) keys the exclusion to an article list (Annex I para 2 / Annex II: critical minerals, energy, pharma, vehicles, etc.) and para (4) to §232-covered articles. Neither §301 list membership nor aluminum membership per se excuses the surcharge, so the pre-fix disjuncts were ungrounded once the module left the witness's five exemplar lines. The proof atoms were NOT touched by this diff, so this is not an excerpt/citation-string (provenance) change — the tested predicate moved to match the already-claimed source.

Anticipated counter-arguments I considered and rejected: (a) "entry_is_line_* are opaque caller inputs, so the module was merely narrow, not wrong" — rejected because the same boolean serves three mutually incompatible statutory memberships inside one file (§122 Annex exclusion, §301 list 1/2/3 gate, and `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a`); at chapter scale at least two of the three uses cannot be source-true, and the PR body states round-2 evaluation showed the coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins". (b) "mechanical regeneration of a generated module" — rejected; formula tokens changed and the statutory stack gained `+ section_232_steel_component_rate`. (c) "reclassify to unrepresented_clause" — the §122 branch already had two disjuncts nominally mapped to the two source exclusions; nothing was added there, only re-grounded. (Note that the *other* rules in this same diff do look like unrepresented_clause: `brazil_section_301_component_rate` and `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` gained missing list-membership gates, and `section_232_steel_component_rate` is new coverage — but the flagged rule_path is section_122.)

For the reviewer, two dedup/quality flags: (1) this commit applies the identical generator-level change to 100 generated chapter modules, so ch51 (module index 50) is not independent evidence — count the defect once per commit, not per module. (2) The fix is partial in this file: `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` (line 1907) and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` (line 1924) still resolve to `entry_is_line_a` / `entry_is_line_b` post-fix, and the new `section_232_steel_component_rate` is emitted with a double-nested `metadata.proof.proof.atoms` at this commit (the PR issue comment says the atoms were later "unwrapped to canonical metadata.proof.atoms", i.e. repaired in a later commit of PR #1300).
